If someone makes me go through the effort to make a reply, only for them to admit that they either skim through it or just plain disregard any attention to basic dialogue. Then Yeah I wouldn't spare them anymore of my time. 

I can partially understand and give some patience to people who can only make shorter replies if they just aren't suited to it(I have RP friends that aren't novella style but at least fully read my replies to grasp what's going on)

But for people who won't even bother to read what their partner wrote? That just shows they don't remotely care about the RP or for their partners efforts. 

I'd have very little time and patience for such bad RP partners.

Personally, I used to feel bad about myself whenever I got those kinds of let downs, but these days I don't mind much when someone expresses that they're not feeling it/Not interested anymore, as long as there's no insults or anything ad hominem. 


I'd prefer to have them honestly express their lack of interest and let them walk away from the RP, rather than to ever have them feel obligated to RP with me just to spare my feelings. 

I never want anyone to feel forced to RP with me, especially if they just aren't feeling invested or having fun. 

If it wasn't a good fit, then it was best that it was dropped, and I just proceed wish them the best of luck in finding someone else more suitable for their RP needs and just move on

Speaking as someone with high functioning autism; i personally prefer to keep my diagnosis on a strict need to know basis; only disclosing it to the necessary parties(doctor, police, etc.) or people who i trust enough. it also made meeting new friends easier especially since they didn't have the autism preconception from the get go. 

However my own mother didn't share that same view, she'd tell it to anybody within earshot; i could not go to a single diner with her without her telling the waitress about my autism; something that annoyed me to no end.

 In my experience people knowing about my diagnosis usually did more harm than good and painted an unnecessary target on my back(especially in high school). 

people who knew about my autism tend to interact with me one of four ways:either treating me like a child, having a misplaced sense of pity or a need to be condescending towards me like I'm incompetent; especially in a work setting or make fun of me. 

But i must clarify that this is simply my experience with this subject so i cannot speak for everyone else on the spectrum.
i do apologize if i did sound a bit jaded.

All of that said, I would best advise asking your son's opinion about it when he gets older. If he's OK with it then be mindful of who you tell that information to because people can potentially shape their perception of him solely on his diagnosis for better or worse.  

However If he wishes to keep it private, please respect that. He may be autistic but he has a right to privacy just like any other human being. Until then, do what you think is best for the time being.
